2026-11-04.subject: Iran Responds to America’s Vote. South Africa Votes on Services. Ukraine Searches the Rubble.
2026-11-04.preview_text: Iran’s response, South Africa’s vote and Ukraine’s rescue, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
2026-11-04.description: Iran interprets America’s election, South Africans vote amid service failures and Ukraine reports a rising strike toll.
2026-11-04.contents_extra: France’s blood storage cyberattack, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Iran Reads America’s Midterm Vote as a Rejection of War
paragraphs: Iran’s chief negotiator said Americans had voted against war after the U.S. midterm elections. BBC News reports Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf endorsed that message on Wednesday. President Donald Trump acknowledged the Iran conflict and higher petrol prices hurt Republicans. He nevertheless said he did not regret launching the joint attack with Israel.

The response did not establish a diplomatic breakthrough. BBC News reports Iran’s supreme leader said U.S. hostility would not change. Indirect talks remained stalled, with Qatar mediating, while the Strait of Hormuz stayed effectively closed, disrupting an important global energy route. Neither the election result nor Tehran’s interpretation ended the conflict.

stories.title: South Africans Vote Amid Anger Over Water and Electricity Failures
paragraphs: South Africans voted in municipal elections Wednesday amid frustration with water outages, power cuts and failing infrastructure. The Guardian reports Johannesburg residents described repeated service breakdowns. The African National Congress faced pressure from several rivals. Polling suggested losses, but those forecasts were not final results or an announcement of who would govern.

The vote chooses councillors rather than directly electing mayors. The Guardian reports parties may need coalition negotiations after the count. Johannesburg had already cycled through 10 mayors in as many years, with unstable local administrations complicating service delivery. Election officials had a week to announce final results before councils moved to select their leadership.

photo.alt: Johannesburg office buildings beneath a pale sky

stories.title: Zelenskyy Reports 40 Confirmed Dead in the Komyshuvakha Strike
paragraphs: At 08:44 EST Wednesday, The Guardian reported Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s update that 40 people were confirmed dead after Monday’s Komyshuvakha school strike. His account put more than 30 people still missing. The building had served as an aid distribution site. Rescue operations continued as officials searched the rubble.

The revised toll followed earlier reports of 31 and then 33 deaths. The Guardian’s morning briefing describes Russian strikes on energy infrastructure alongside the rescue effort. Power stations and substations were hit across Ukraine. Diplomatic preparations continued for talks in Abu Dhabi, but those plans did not halt attacks or resolve the humanitarian emergency.

photo.alt: Kyiv buildings seen through leafy trees

deep_dive.title: A Cyberattack on French Blood Storage Shows the Stakes of Connected Equipment
paragraphs: What happened. France’s national blood service said hackers raised temperatures at three cold stores containing blood products. The Guardian reports alarms allowed technicians to intervene before the products were compromised. The attack occurred overnight Monday and affected facilities run by contractors. Stored products, including plasma bags, were moved to other sites as a precaution.

Why it matters. Blood products depend on controlled storage conditions before reaching patients. The Guardian reports the French service supplies more than 1,900 hospitals. The incident followed refrigeration attacks on supermarkets in several European countries. Connected control systems let operators monitor equipment remotely, but unpatched vulnerabilities can also expose those systems to hostile interference.

What each side says. The blood service said it had alerted France’s cybersecurity agency and health ministry. The Guardian reports European authorities were discussing a collective response. No motive was known and nobody had claimed responsibility. Speculation about a state actor or an individual hacker remained speculation, not an established attribution of the attacks.

What comes next. The service said monitoring had been reinforced across its equipment. The Guardian reports the affected blood products had been relocated. Investigators still needed to establish responsibility and whether incidents shared a cause. Wednesday’s reporting showed successful intervention at these stores, not proof that all connected refrigeration systems were secure against future attacks.

photo.alt: Hands using a pipette beside laboratory tubes

trivia.question: Which country’s national blood service reported the cold store cyberattack?
trivia.explanation: France is correct. Its national blood service said alarms protected products at three affected cold stores.

2026-11-05.subject: Europe Faces Flight Bomb Hoaxes. Hormuz Shipping Remains at Risk. Britain Raises Interest Rates.
2026-11-05.preview_text: Flight hoaxes, tanker risks and Britain’s rate increase, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
2026-11-05.description: Bomb threats disrupt European flights, Iran claims more tanker incidents and Britain raises its base rate to 4%.
2026-11-05.contents_extra: Joshua Wong’s new prison sentence, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Bomb Hoaxes Force Emergency Landings and Military Escorts Across Europe
paragraphs: Bomb threats disrupted flights across Europe Thursday, prompting emergency landings, searches and military escorts. AP reports more than a dozen flights were confirmed targets. Inspections had found no hazardous or suspicious materials. An Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome landed at a French military base with everyone aboard safe.

The threats’ origin remained uncertain. AP reviewed an email claiming to come from an antifeminist group, but did not establish who was responsible. European transport officials activated aviation security information sharing. They said investigations continued and it was too early to determine whether the incidents were linked or involved a cyberattack.

photo.alt: A silhouetted traveller waits inside an airport

stories.title: Iran Claims More Tanker Mine Strikes While Maritime Monitors Report an Attack
paragraphs: Iranian forces said more tankers were damaged near the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday. Al Jazeera reports Iranian statements describing mine strikes and fires. Those claims did not independently establish the number of vessels hit. The waterway normally carries about a fifth of global oil consumption, making disruptions internationally significant.

A separate report described an attack off Qatar, with responsibility not immediately claimed. Al Jazeera reports British maritime monitors said two projectiles struck a tanker Wednesday night. Qatar continued mediation efforts, but military warnings persisted. The reported incidents showed shipping remained exposed despite diplomatic proposals aimed at ending the conflict.

photo.alt: A red tanker viewed from above

stories.title: The Bank of England Raises Its Base Rate to 4%
paragraphs: The Bank of England raised interest rates Thursday for the first time in more than 3 years. The Guardian reports the base rate increased from 3.75% to 4%. Eight policymakers supported that increase. A ninth preferred a larger rise as the bank confronted inflation linked to higher energy costs.

The decision increases pressure on borrowers while potentially improving some savings returns. The Guardian reports Governor Andrew Bailey signalled another increase could be needed. He did not describe a long sequence of rises as inevitable. The bank’s inflation outlook depended heavily on the Iran conflict and whether lower energy prices persisted.

photo.alt: Green fields and houses in the English countryside

deep_dive.title: Joshua Wong’s New Sentence Extends Hong Kong’s National Security Crackdown
paragraphs: What happened. A Hong Kong court sentenced activist Joshua Wong to 10 years in prison Thursday after his guilty plea to foreign collusion. The Guardian reports the sentence runs alongside the remaining term of an earlier conviction. It was his second prosecution under the national security law, which Beijing introduced after the city’s mass protests.

Why it matters. Wong became internationally known during Hong Kong’s 2014 democracy demonstrations. The Guardian reports he had already spent nearly 6 years in detention. Before this sentence, he had been due for release in January 2027. The new case concerned efforts to encourage foreign sanctions and related measures against China, including social media activity.

What each side says. The judge described Wong’s conduct as grave and part of a scheme involving foreign governments. The Guardian reports rights groups said the law punishes peaceful dissent. The U.S. consulate condemned the sentence and sought his release. China’s foreign ministry rejected outside criticism and urged respect for sovereignty and Hong Kong’s legal system.

What comes next. The sentence leaves one of the democracy movement’s most recognizable figures facing years more in prison. The Guardian reports diplomats and supporters attended the hearing. The dispute over the law’s purpose remains unresolved. Beijing describes it as necessary for stability, while critics say it has suppressed opposition and weakened civil society.

photo.alt: Hong Kong’s illuminated waterfront at night

trivia.question: What base rate did the Bank of England set on November 5?
trivia.explanation: 4% is correct. The bank raised its rate from 3.75% on November 5.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine Agree a Prisoner Exchange but Report No Major Peace Breakthrough
paragraphs: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large prisoner exchange Wednesday as talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a major peace breakthrough. AP reports both delegations confirmed the planned swap. Russia’s negotiator described the agreement as in principle. The number of prisoners and practical arrangements had not been finalized.

The humanitarian agreement did not settle disputes over territory or security guarantees. AP reports U.S. envoys planned separate meetings with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy. European participation remained contested, with Moscow opposing a direct role. The talks were the delegations’ first meeting in 9 months, while missile and drone attacks continued.

photo.alt: Illuminated Abu Dhabi mosque reflected in water

stories.title: Climate Leaders Warn That War Cannot Put Emissions Action on Hold
paragraphs: World leaders began two days of COP31 speeches in Antalya on Wednesday. Reuters reports the summit seeks progress despite wars, inflation and other competing crises. U.N. Secretary General António Guterres said the climate crisis was outrunning the international response. Turkey wants electrification at the centre of a final agreement.

The proposal would raise electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035. Reuters reports critics want a clearer plan to reduce fossil fuel use. The United States stayed away for a second year. Barbados’s Mia Mottley called for cheaper finance and disaster clauses in international loans, highlighting vulnerable countries’ demands.

photo.alt: Harbour with Turkish flag and mountains

stories.title: Indonesia’s Lawmakers Prepare a Motion as Gibran’s Resignation Plans Advance
paragraphs: Indonesia’s vice presidential crisis advanced on Wednesday as lawmakers prepared a parliamentary motion. Antara reports Deputy Speaker Saan Mustopa planned to submit it to Thursday’s plenary. The proposal had support from 120 legislators. Projo leader Budi Arie Setiadi also confirmed Gibran Rakabuming Raka’s resignation plans when contacted by the agency.

Formal completion remained distinct from those statements at this edition’s cutoff. The palace had confirmed Gibran’s intention to step down on Tuesday, following a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto. The dispute concerned his educational qualifications. A Supreme Court ruling invalidated his equivalency certificate, while Gibran sought another opportunity to defend his diplomas in court.

photo.alt: Central Jakarta skyline seen from Monas

deep_dive.title: How an Alleged Fairford Plot Tested Security Around a U.S. Bomber Base
paragraphs: What happened. U.S. prosecutors unsealed charges Tuesday against three men accused of an international attack campaign. NPR reports the indictment includes a September plot against RAF Fairford, a British base hosting American bombers. Prosecutors linked the defendants to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and Kata’ib Hezbollah. The charges describe allegations, not findings of guilt.

Why it matters. Fairford serves as a forward operating base for U.S. strategic bombers. NPR reports associates allegedly filmed its perimeter and obtained vans and fuel drums. Prosecutors say the vehicles carried false commercial branding. Two were stopped near the base at a security roadblock, and authorities seized all three the following morning.

What each side says. The indictment alleges the network continued operating after one defendant entered U.S. custody in May. The Guardian reports prosecutors say coded family calls transmitted instructions. The alleged preparations included researching chemical accelerants and metal objects for shrapnel. The Fairford allegations form part of a broader case involving attacks on Jewish communities.

What comes next. The criminal case must test prosecutors’ account rather than treating the indictment as a verdict. NPR notes British authorities had separately charged two men over the incident. Neither government confirmed a reported recent aircraft relocation was caused by an Iranian threat. Britain’s defence ministry said aircraft routinely move for operational reasons.

photo.alt: Stone cottages in an English village

trivia.explanation: 11:00 is correct. The Armistice took effect at 11:00 on 11 November 1918.

2026-11-12.contents_extra: Spain’s general strike over housing, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Gibran Submits His Resignation as Indonesia’s Vice President
paragraphs: Gibran Rakabuming Raka submitted his resignation to Indonesia’s parliamentary assembly leaders on Thursday. Antara reports Speaker Ahmad Muzani read the letter to journalists after a 20 minute meeting. The letter gave no specific reason. Gibran said he acted voluntarily for the nation and the smooth functioning of government.

The assembly speaker said the vice presidential post was now vacant. Antara reports the assembly would hold a joint session and notify President Prabowo Subianto. Muzani said a 14 day nomination period would follow that notification. The formal letter follows Tuesday’s stated intention to resign amid a dispute over Gibran’s educational qualifications.

stories.title: Witkoff Says Another Ukraine Talks Round Is Agreed After Meeting Putin
paragraphs: U.S. envoys completed their meeting with Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday. The Guardian’s dated live coverage reports Steve Witkoff said another trilateral round was agreed. He said Europeans would join the next meeting. Witkoff and Jared Kushner then left Moscow en route to Dublin for consultations with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

The agreement to meet again was not a peace settlement. The Guardian reports Putin repeated demands over occupied territory and opposed foreign peacekeepers. The Kremlin called the talks useful and said the process would continue. ABC News describes unresolved differences over territory and security guarantees after the earlier Abu Dhabi discussions.

stories.title: Iran Warns of Wider Retaliation as Israeli Strike Preparations Are Reported
paragraphs: Iran warned it could target bases beyond the region if the United States launched another war. Al Jazeera attributes the warning to security chief Mohsen Rezaei. The report followed Israeli broadcaster KAN’s account of military preparations for a possible attack. Those reported directives did not establish that any attack had begun.

The preparations also exposed a dispute within Israeli politics. Al Jazeera reports Gadi Eisenkot urged caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to avoid unnecessary operations. Eisenkot is trying to form the next government. Washington continued to emphasize economic pressure and diplomacy, while Tehran said trust remained an obstacle to agreement over the Strait of Hormuz.

deep_dive.title: Spain’s First General Strike in 14 Years Puts Housing at the Centre of the Election
paragraphs: What happened. Spain held a general strike over housing costs on Wednesday, its first in 14 years. BBC News reports large marches in Madrid and Barcelona. Some Barcelona protesters set bins alight and smashed windows, and police used tear gas. The housing demonstrations came less than 3 weeks before a snap national election.

Why it matters. Rising rents have put housing at the centre of the campaign. BBC News reports a 50 square metre Madrid flat averaged 1,170 euros monthly in October, citing Idealista. That figure describes advertised local rents, not every tenant’s bill. The strike brought tenants’ groups and workers’ unions together around demands for more affordable homes.

What each side says. Sánchez and his ministers encouraged workers to strike for affordable housing. BBC News reports the opposition People’s Party accused the government of exploiting the action for electoral gain. Union leaders described participation as strong, while a business association called the protest political. Parliament’s failure to approve housing reform had prompted the snap election.

What comes next. Spaniards vote on 29 November, with housing costs now a central campaign issue. BBC News reports transport and other public services faced serious disruption during the strike. Its reporting described dozens of arrests, not a final nationwide count. Participation figures and Wednesday’s clashes did not determine the election’s outcome or settle the housing policy dispute.

trivia.question: How many days must pass before Kenya’s Ebola outbreak can be declared over?
trivia.explanation: 42 days is correct. BBC News reports the countdown follows the final patient’s negative test and discharge.
